title: SKU Splitter: pricing journey and per-usage attribution panel
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design a compact, role-aware 'SKU Splitter' panel inside Redwood Console that surfaces token-level cost attribution, SKU-aware pricing bands, and exportable datasets. The panel should support quick price-sensitivity simulations for engineering and finance users, allow CSV/Parquet export, and integrate with existing rollout controls so cost-affecting changes can be previewed before publishing. Focus on dense information presentation for power users while providing accessible summary views for non-technical stakeholders.
acceptance_criteria: Panel placed under Cost > Attribution with a compact header, summary row, and expandable detail table
Per-message and per-token breakdowns available with SKU attribution (model variant, quantization, region, tier)
Export presets: Summary CSV, Raw Events CSV, and Aggregated Parquet; export triggers background job with status toast and link to export history
Simulate pricing: slider/controls to toggle batch sizes, quantization profile, and compute tier; simulation updates cost estimates within 1 second for sampled windows
Role filters: Billing Admins see raw cost columns; Developers see token-level technical columns; Finance sees currency-normalized totals
Performance: UI supports lazy-loading and server-side sampling for >1M events; pagination and 'sample vs full export' explanation visible
Accessibility: keyboard navigation, screen-reader labels for table columns, contrast-compliant color palette
design_notes: Primary visual is a compact table with a header band showing total spend, unit cost, and 7d trend sparkline. Detail rows represent SKU slices (model@quant, region, deployment tier). On expand, each slice shows top prompt templates, median latency, token distribution histogram and attribution percent. Pricing simulation UI uses inline chips and a dismissible 'what-if' banner. For very large time ranges, the panel shows a row-level sampling badge and an estimated sampling error. We recommend pre-aggregated endpoints for daily/hourly buckets and a streaming preview endpoint for the 'Simulate' feature. Use existing Console colors and microcomponents; introduce a new 'export job' toast pattern for long-running CSV/Parquet exports.
decisions: Use sampled preview for simulations by default; full exports require background job
Show SKU slices ordered by spend descending with stable pagination
Keep simulation sliders client-side but fetch recalculated estimates via a lightweight sampling API to keep estimates accurate
tasks: Finalize Figma prototype for compact & expanded states (design)
Add API contract for /costs/sku-slices with sampling params (eng)
Implement export-job flow and history link (eng + infra)
E2E accessibility pass and keyboard focus map (design)
Add unit tests for pricing-simulation inputs and result staleness (eng)
